en: to unite; to combine; to join

examples.en: The two companies combine into one.
Water and oil don't combine.

examples.ko: 두 재료를 결합하면 새로운 맛이 나요.
examples.en: Combining the two ingredients gives a new flavor.

examples.ko: 한글은 자음과 모음을 결합해서 글자를 만들어요.
examples.en: Hangul builds letters by combining consonants and vowels.
The combined shape is interesting.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 생각을 결합할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can we combine different ideas?

explain: 서로 다른 둘이 합쳐져 하나가 될 때 써요. '합치다'보다 딱딱해서 과학, 기술, 문법 설명에 나와요. 'A와 B를 결합하다'나 'A가 B와 결합하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The two parts are firmly joined together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합쳐진 결과나 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the result or state of being combined.

phrases.en: This app combines photos and music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합치는 두 대상을 함께 말하는 기본 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pattern naming the two things that are combined.

phrases.en: We merge the two classes into one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결합하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 결합하다 and used more in everyday talk.

explain_en: Joining parts or elements into one thing (음악과 기술을 결합하다) Use it when two different things join into one. It is stiffer than '합치다' and appears in science, technology, and grammar explanations. The patterns are 'A와 B를 결합하다' and 'A가 B와 결합하다'.

dis.h: join parts or elements into one
gh: groups form an alliance or league
casual: band together, or clump up
bind together tightly by a common bond
stand in solidarity for a cause

p.n: 연합하다 is for groups allying, not for joining object parts.

examples.en: The kids chatter nonstop in the classroom.
Sparrows have been chirping outside the window since morning.

examples.ko: 동생은 학교에서 있었던 일을 신나게 재잘거렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling excitedly chattered about what happened at school.

examples.ko: 뒷자리 친구들이 재잘거리는 소리에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up from the sound of friends chattering in the back seats.

examples.ko: 조용히 해야 하는데 자꾸 재잘거리게 돼요.
examples.en: I'm supposed to be quiet, but I keep ending up chattering.

examples.ko: 딸이 하루 종일 재잘거려서 집이 시끌시끌해요.
examples.en: My daughter chatters all day long, so the house is lively and noisy.

explain: 주로 아이나 새가 높은 목소리로 끊임없이 말하거나 지저귈 때 써요. '떠들다'는 시끄럽다는 느낌이 강하고, '재잘거리다'는 귀엽고 정겨운 느낌이 있어요. '재잘대다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: The children chatter during break time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재잘거리다'와 거의 같고 말할 때 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 재잘거리다, a bit more casual in speech.

phrases.en: My little sister chatters on about school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끊임없이 말하는 모습을 나타내는 흉내말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An imitative word showing nonstop chatter.

phrases.en: I hear birds twittering outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

explain_en: It is mainly used for children or birds talking or chirping nonstop in a high voice. '떠들다' feels more like 'making noise', while '재잘거리다' has a cute, warm feel. '재잘대다' is used almost the same way.

t90.ax: The kids chatter nonstop in the classroom.

examples.ko: 교실 여기저기서 킥킥 웃음을 참는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: Here and there in the classroom came the sound of people holding back giggles.
Someone behind me snickered.

examples.ko: 둘이 귓속말을 하며 킥킥 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are whispering and giggling.
I tried to hold in my laughter, but giggles slipped out.
I giggle to myself while reading comics.
I heard a snicker and looked back.

explain: 웃음을 참다가 짧게 새어 나오는 소리예요. '키득키득'과 비슷한데 '킥킥'이 더 짧고 빠른 느낌이에요. 몰래 웃거나 놀리듯 웃을 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I giggled with my friend behind the teacher's back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '킥킥'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 킥킥.

phrases.en: The kids in the back row are giggling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음이 계속 이어진다는 뜻을 더한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the sense that the laughing continues.

phrases.en: The kids played pranks, giggling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '킥킥'보다 조금 더 길게 이어지는 웃음소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A giggle that goes on a bit longer than 킥킥.

explain_en: Short stifled laugh, trying not to be heard, like in class. It is the short sound of laughter slipping out when you try to hold it in. It is similar to '키득키득', but '킥킥' feels shorter and quicker. It is often used for laughing secretly or teasingly.

examples.en: Mom pats the crying baby's back.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 어깨를 토닥이며 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend comforted me by patting my shoulder.
I slowly patted the child's chest to put him to sleep.
Please pat my back and tell me it's okay.
The teacher patted my head and walked by.

examples.ko: 수고했다고 서로 어깨를 토닥이는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see them patting each other's shoulders to say 'good job.'

explain: 손으로 부드럽게 가볍게 두드린다는 느낌이고, 위로하거나 달래거나 칭찬할 때 많이 써요. 세게 치는 '때리다'와는 달리 따뜻한 마음이 담겨 있어요. 보통 등, 어깨, 머리처럼 몸에 쓰고 '토닥토닥'이라는 흉내말도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 엄마가 제 등을 토닥토닥 두드려 줬어요.
phrases.en: My mom patted my back gently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부드럽게 두드리는 소리와 모습을 나타내는 흉내말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A mimetic word for the sound and look of gentle patting.

phrases.en: I patted the child gently until he fell asleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달래거나 위로해 주는 마음이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows more clearly the intent to soothe or comfort.

phrases.en: I sing while patting the baby gently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 번 계속 토닥이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes patting gently again and again.

explain_en: It carries a feel of gently tapping with the hand, and is often used to comfort, soothe or praise someone. Unlike '때리다' (hit), it carries warmth. It is usually used on the back, shoulder or head, and the sound word '토닥토닥' is also common.

t90.ax: Mom pats the crying baby's back.

examples.en: Please join our gathering after work.

examples.ko: 친구들은 먼저 출발했고 저는 나중에 합류했어요.
examples.en: My friends left first and I joined them later.

examples.ko: 두 길이 만나는 곳에서 팀이 합류할 거예요.
examples.en: The team will join up where the two roads meet.

examples.ko: 새로 합류한 직원이 일을 빨리 배워요.
examples.en: The newly joined employee learns the work quickly.

examples.ko: 내일 오후 회의에 저도 합류해도 될까요?
examples.en: May I join tomorrow afternoon's meeting too?

examples.ko: 두 강이 합류하는 곳을 보러 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to see where the two rivers join.

explain: '합류하다'는 이미 움직이는 무리나 길에 나중에 들어와 합쳐지는 것을 말해요. '참가하다'는 행사나 대회에 들어가는 느낌이고, '같이하다'는 처음부터 함께하는 느낌이에요. 사람, 길, 강에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I'll join you as soon as work is done.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 따라가겠다고 약속할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to promise you will catch up later.

phrases.en: I joined my friends' gathering later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼저 시작한 무리에 늦게 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when joining a group that started earlier.

phrases.en: Please join us for dinner tonight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음부터 함께한다는 느낌이에요. '합류하다'와 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like being together from the start, unlike 합류하다.

explain_en: To join a person, group, or path already moving (친구들과 합류하다) 합류하다 means joining a group or road that is already moving. 참가하다 is for entering an event or contest, and 같이하다 feels like doing it together from the start. It works for people, roads, and rivers.

dis.h: meet up and join a group or path
gh: business joining an association or franchise

p.n: 합류 is physically joining up with a group; 가입 is formally signing up.

t90.ax: Please join our gathering after work.

en: to dig out; to gouge out; to scrape out

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서 코를 후비는 건 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: Picking your nose in front of people is not polite.
My ear hurt while I was digging in it.

examples.ko: 아이가 모래를 손으로 후벼 파고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is digging into the sand with his hands.
I picked between my teeth with a toothpick.
When I rummaged in my pocket, a coin came out.
Don't pick at the wound; just leave it.

explain: 손가락이나 뾰족한 도구로 좁은 곳 안쪽을 긁어내듯 건드릴 때 써요. '코를 후비다', '귀를 후비다'로 가장 많이 쓰여요. '파다'는 땅을 팔 때도 쓰지만, '후비다'는 작은 구멍 안쪽을 건드리는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Please don't keep picking your nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좁은 곳 안쪽을 건드리지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to dig at a small, narrow spot.

phrases.en: I scooped out the watermelon with a spoon and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속을 긁어내듯이 파낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for scooping out the inside.

phrases.en: My younger brother has a habit of picking his nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자주 하는 습관을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a habit someone often does.

explain_en: It describes poking or scraping inside a narrow spot with a finger or a pointed tool. Its most common use is 코를 후비다 and 귀를 후비다. 파다 can mean digging the ground, while 후비다 feels like touching the inside of a small hole.

examples.ko: 가을에는 단감이 맛있어서 매일 하나씩 먹어요.
examples.en: Sweet persimmons are delicious in fall, so I eat one every day.
I bought a box of sweet persimmons at the market.

examples.ko: 단감은 홍시와 달리 딱딱할 때 먹어도 달아요.
examples.en: Unlike soft persimmons, sweet persimmons are sweet even when they're firm.
There is a sweet persimmon tree in my maternal grandmother's yard.
I peeled a sweet persimmon and gave it to the child.

examples.ko: 이 단감이 크고 달아서 선물하기 좋아요.
examples.en: These sweet persimmons are big and sweet, so they're good for gifts.

explain: 떫지 않아서 딱딱한 채로 깎아 먹는 감이에요. 말랑하게 익은 감은 '홍시', 말린 감은 '곶감'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 가을 과일로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I peeled a sweet persimmon and ate it with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 딱딱한 단감은 껍질을 깎아서 먹는다는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing because firm sweet persimmons are peeled before eating.

phrases.en: I got a box of sweet persimmons as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수를 세는 말과 함께 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A usage with a counting word.

phrases.en: My grandmother likes soft ripe persimmons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단감과 달리 말랑하게 익은 감이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '단감', this is a soft, fully ripened persimmon.

explain_en: It is a persimmon that is not astringent, so you peel and eat it while still firm. A soft ripe persimmon is '홍시' and a dried one is '곶감', so they are different things. It often comes up as a fall fruit.

examples.en: I rolled out and made the dumpling wrappers myself.
I bought a pack of dumpling wrappers at the supermarket.
The wrapper is so thin that it keeps tearing.
Lightly brush water on the edge of the wrapper.
I made a snack out of the leftover wrappers.

examples.ko: 이 집은 만두피가 쫄깃해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This place is popular because its dumpling skin is chewy.

explain: '만두 껍질'이라고도 말해요. 안에 넣는 '만두소'와 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The dumpling wrapper is thin, so it tears easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만두피'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 만두피, widely used in daily speech.

phrases.en: I rolled out dumpling wrappers from flour dough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반죽을 얇게 펴서 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for rolling dough thin to make wrappers.

phrases.en: Wrap the filling in a dumpling wrapper and steam it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만두소를 피로 감싸는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes wrapping the filling in the wrapper.
phrases.en_equiv: to wrap in a dumpling wrapper

explain_en: People also say '만두 껍질'. It is handy to memorize it as a pair with '만두소', the filling inside.

examples.en: I added a little celery to the salad.

examples.ko: 셀러리는 향이 강해서 안 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Celery has a strong smell, so some people don't eat it.
Please slice the celery stalks thinly.
I bought a bunch of celery at the supermarket.
I drink celery juice every morning.
Celery and onions go into this soup.

explain: 표준 표기는 '셀러리'예요. '샐러리'라고 쓰면 월급을 뜻하는 영어 salary가 떠올라 헷갈릴 수 있으니 조심하세요. 한국 음식에는 자주 안 쓰지만 샐러드나 주스에 많이 넣어요.

phrases.en: I drink celery juice every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 셀러리를 음료로 마실 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when celery is drunk as a beverage.

phrases.example: 셀러리 줄기를 얇게 썰어서 샐러드에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: I sliced the celery stalk thinly and put it in the salad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리가 주로 먹는 부분이 줄기예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The stalk is the part we mainly eat.

phrases.en: I chop the celery before cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 준비할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when preparing food.

explain_en: The standard spelling is '셀러리'. Writing '샐러리' can be confused with the English word salary, so be careful. It is not common in traditional Korean cooking, but it is often used in salads and juices.

examples.en: A lot of spices go into Indian cooking.

examples.ko: 저는 향신료 냄새가 강한 음식이 조금 힘들어요.
examples.en: Food with a strong spice smell is a bit hard for me.
I sprinkled spices before grilling the meat.
Pepper and cinnamon are typical spices.

examples.ko: 향신료는 쓰는 양에 따라 맛이 많이 달라져요.
examples.en: With spices, the taste changes a lot depending on how much you use.

examples.ko: 한국 음식은 향신료보다 양념을 많이 써요.
examples.en: Korean food uses more seasoning than spices.

explain: 후추, 계피, 카레 가루처럼 향이 강한 재료를 통틀어 말해요. 한국 음식 이야기에서는 '양념'이라는 말을 더 자주 쓰는데, 양념에는 간장, 고춧가루, 마늘까지 들어가서 범위가 더 넓어요.

phrases.en: I added a little spice to the dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에 향이 나는 재료를 더할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for adding aromatic ingredients to food.

phrases.en: This curry has a strong spice smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식에서 향신료의 향이 세게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the aroma of spices in food is strong.

phrases.en: Seasoning is important in Korean food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간장, 마늘 같은 것까지 포함해서 범위가 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also includes things like soy sauce and garlic.

explain_en: It covers strongly scented ingredients such as pepper, cinnamon, and curry powder. When talking about Korean food, '양념' is used more often, and it is wider because it includes soy sauce, red pepper powder, and garlic.

examples.en: You peel the shell of pumpkin seeds before eating them.
I roasted pumpkin seeds and ate them as a snack.
I heard pumpkin seeds have many nutrients that are good for the body.
Grandmother dried the pumpkin seeds and set them aside.
I sprinkled pumpkin seeds on top of the salad.

examples.ko: 호박씨 껍질을 까는 데 손이 많이 가요.
examples.en: Peeling pumpkin seeds takes a lot of effort.

explain: 볶아서 간식이나 안주로, 또 샐러드나 죽에 넣어 먹어요. 껍질을 까서 먹는 씨앗이라 '호박씨를 까다'라고 해요. 이 '까다'가 아래 관용 표현에도 쓰여요.

phrases.example: 얌전한 줄 알았는데 뒤에서 호박씨를 깠어요.
phrases.en: I thought he was quiet, but he was up to something behind my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 얌전하고 아무것도 모르는 척하면서 뒤에서 몰래 딴짓을 하거나 제 이익을 챙길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts quiet and innocent on the surface but secretly does something else or looks after their own interests behind the scenes.
phrases.en_equiv: do something sneaky behind one's back

explain_en: They are roasted and eaten as a snack, or added to salads and porridge. Since you peel the shell, the verb is '호박씨를 까다'. That same '까다' is used in the idiom below.

en: to be straight; to be upright; to be stiff

examples.en: Even though Grandfather is old, his back is still straight.

examples.ko: 아기가 벽을 잡고 꼿꼿이 서서 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is standing upright holding the wall, smiling.
Her posture is upright like a model's, so she stands out.
I sat up straight during the interview.

examples.ko: 그분은 끝까지 꼿꼿하게 자기 뜻을 지켰어요.
examples.en: He firmly held to his own will to the end.

examples.ko: 허리가 꼿꼿하지 않아서 거울을 자주 봐요.
examples.en: My back isn't straight, so I check the mirror often.

explain: 몸이나 막대가 구부러지지 않고 곧을 때 써요. 사람의 태도에 쓰면 굽히지 않고 당당하다는 뜻인데, 때로는 좀 뻣뻣하다는 느낌도 있어요.

phrases.example: 선생님은 항상 꼿꼿한 자세로 앉아 계세요.
phrases.en: The teacher always sits with an upright posture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '꼿꼿한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '꼿꼿한' when describing a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 병사가 문 앞에 꼿꼿하게 서 있어요.
phrases.en: The soldier stands straight in front of the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 굽히지 않고 곧게 서 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes standing without bending, with a straight back.

phrases.en: My grandmother's back was straight when she was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼿꼿하다'의 과거형이라서 예전의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense, used to describe how someone or something used to be.

explain_en: Rigidly upright posture or firm attitude, often of older people. It describes a body or stick that does not bend. For a person's attitude it means firm and unyielding, though it can sometimes sound a little stiff.

t90.ax: I sat up straight during the interview.

en: comfortably; in a relaxed manner; at ease

examples.en: On weekend mornings I drink coffee at a leisurely pace.
We have plenty of time, so please wait calmly.

examples.ko: 그는 소파에 느긋이 앉아서 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: He sat comfortably on the sofa and read a book.
I took a relaxed walk and looked around the neighborhood.
You don't need to rush; you can get ready at ease.

examples.ko: 휴가 때는 느긋이 늦잠을 자고 싶어요.
examples.en: On vacation I want to sleep in leisurely.

explain: 서두르지 않고 마음이 편한 모습을 말해요. '천천히'는 속도 중심이고, '느긋이'는 마음의 여유가 느껴지는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '느긋하게'도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Rest comfortably on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느긋이'와 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 느긋이 and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: He has a relaxed personality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않는 성격이나 상태를 말하는 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective for a calm, unhurried personality or state.

phrases.en: I took the test with a relaxed mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음에 여유가 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a calm and unhurried state of mind.

explain_en: It describes being unhurried with a calm mind. '천천히' focuses on speed, while '느긋이' suggests a relaxed state of mind. '느긋하게' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The teacher is expressionless today.
He answered with a blank face, which was a little scary.

examples.ko: 그녀는 아무 일도 없었다는 듯 무표정했어요.
examples.en: She looked blank as if nothing had happened.

examples.ko: 무표정하게 앉아 있어도 속으로는 떨고 있었어요.
examples.en: Even though I sat there blank-faced, inside I was shaking.
Why are you so expressionless?

examples.ko: 사진 찍을 때 너무 무표정할 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: You don't have to be so blank when taking a photo.

explain: '무표정한 얼굴'처럼 얼굴 앞에서 꾸미는 쓰임이 가장 많아요. 무뚝뚝한 사람은 성격 이야기이고, 무표정하다는 그때의 얼굴만 말해요. 놀랍거나 화난 일이 있어도 겉으로 안 드러낼 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling looks expressionless today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보이는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for how someone appears on the outside.

phrases.en: He was sitting there with no expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 방법을 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describing how someone does something.

phrases.example: 저 사람은 말이 적지만 무표정하지 않아요.
phrases.en: That person says little but isn't expressionless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대로 얼굴에 감정이 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say feelings do show on the face.

explain_en: The most common use is before 얼굴: 무표정한 얼굴. 무뚝뚝하다 is about personality, while 무표정하다 only describes the face at that moment. It is often used when someone shows nothing despite being surprised or angry.

en: color tone; feel of colors; sense of color

examples.en: The colors in this photo are really pretty.
That painter has an excellent sense of color.
I bought a bag in warm tones.
If you use a filter, the color tone changes.
In interior design, matching the color tones is important.

examples.ko: 저는 이 그림의 색감이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the color feel of this painting.

explain: 색 자체가 아니라 색이 주는 전체 느낌과 분위기를 말해요. 그래서 '빨간색'보다는 '따뜻한 색감', '차분한 색감'처럼 말해요. 사진, 그림, 옷, 인테리어를 평가할 때 일상에서도 자주 써요. 비슷한 말 '색깔'은 그냥 어떤 색인지를 말해요.

phrases.en: The room has warm colors, so it feels comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 주는 전체 분위기를 말할 때 이렇게 꾸며서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier used to describe the overall mood of colors.

phrases.example: 사진을 찍을 때 색감을 살리고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to bring out the colors when taking photos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진이나 그림에서 색의 느낌이 잘 보이게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the feel of the colors stand out in a photo or painting.

phrases.en: The color of the clothes is different from the photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: '색감'은 느낌 전체이고, '색깔'은 빨강, 파랑 같은 색 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 색감 is the overall feel; 색깔 is the color itself, like red or blue.

explain_en: Overall impression of colors in a picture, photo or design. It refers to the overall feel and mood that colors give, not the color itself, so Koreans say 따뜻한 색감 or 차분한 색감 rather than just red. It is common in daily talk about photos, paintings, clothes, and interiors. 색깔 simply tells which color it is.
